newsitem.title: USA: CBOT board approves changes in grain delivery pts.
newsitem.headline: CBOT board approves changes in grain delivery pts.

text.p: The board of directors of Chicago Board of Trade approved proposed changes in delivery locations for its grain and soybean futures contracts and sent the matter to the membership for a vote, CBOT said.

The changes include addition of Milwaukee, Wisconsin, and Northern Illinois River as delivery points, deletion of St Louis as a delivery point, and changes in the Toledo delivery differentials and load-out requirements, the exchange said.
The changes were approved at the board's monthly meeting Tuesday and endorse the CBOT's Grain Storage Task Force plan, except for its call for an East Central Illinois delivery.

"In this modified form, the proposed changes still will allow CBOT agricultural contracts to adapt to changing economic realities and will address the fundamental issue of diminished regular capacity in the delivery system," the exchange said in a statement.

"At the same time, the modified porposal addresses concerns about the detrimental effects on spread trading and is simpler in overall terms than the package originally presented by the Task Force," CBOT said.
Under the approved proposals, corn and soybeans can be delivered at Milwaukee at par value to the CBOT price.

For Northern Illinois River locations, regular warehouses located on the river north of Creve Coeur (or the Peoria Locka and Dam at mile 157.7) are eligible for delivery for corn at par value and soybeans at a 4-cent-per-bushel discount.

For delivery at Toledo, Ohio, discounts for delivery of corn are decreased to 2 cents per bushel from 3 cents and for soybeans to 4 cents per bushel from 8 cents. In addition, wheat can now be delivered at par against the CBOT contract instead of at a 2 cents per bushel discount.
St Louis will be discontinued as a delivery point for CBOT corn, soybeans and wheat, according to the CBOT statement.
The proposals also modify load-out requirements at the locations for CBOT contracts. For Chicago delivery, barge load-out requirement was reduced to 2 barges per day from 3.
At taker's option, warehousemen can load 4 barges a day with 2 barges at elevators in Chicago/Burns Harbor and 2 on the Illinois Waterway System north of Creve Coeur, it said.

For Milwaukee, load-out discounts were set at 8 cents a bushel for corn or soybeans on rail or barge but par for grain loaded on a vessel. At taker's option, warehousemen can load 4 barges a day on the Illinois Waterway between Creve Coeur and Chicago/Burns Harbor, the CBOT said.

For the Northern Illinois River, warehousemen must load a minimum 4 barges per day against cancelled receipts at his warehouse and is not obligated to load railcars. Loading must begin within 3 business days following receipt of loading orders on 1 day of constructive placement at his warehouse.
Storage charges at eligible river elevators for corn, soybeans and wheat must not exceed 1/10 of 1 cent per bushel per day, the CBOT said.
Warehousemen on the river must deliver 5,000 bushel receipts against grain futures contracts in multiples of 50,000 or 55,000 bushels.

The CBOT said it was also increasing the net worth requirement for all regular grain warehouses to $10,000 per contract of regular capacity from $5,000 and said all such warehouses must have net worth of $40 million or more.
The CBOT has not yet set a date for a membership vote on plan, pending briefings to members this week.
